instructions: Add one confirmed row per concrete evidence item. Cite canonical source files, copy verifier excerpts verbatim, and judge source presence separately from recovery.

criteria.criterion: Access the specified NIST Chemistry WebBook record for water (ID=C7732185)
criteria.description: Information must be taken from the NIST Chemistry WebBook record for water corresponding to the context URL (ID=C7732185). Full credit if the agent clearly uses that record OR if the agent attempts to access it but the page is inaccessible (blocked, down, CAPTCHA) and the agent clearly reports this. Partial credit if the agent uses NIST WebBook but provenance is ambiguous. No credit if values are clearly from non-NIST sources or a different substance/record when the specified record was accessible.

screenshot_context.verifier_evidence: Screenshot 1 (latest that shows identity header) clearly displays the NIST Chemistry WebBook compound page titled “Water” with “CAS Registry Number: 7732-18-5,” consistent with the specified record context (water, ID=C7732185). Action history only shows scrolling, but the screenshot provides direct page identity. Screenshot 2 shows navigation links but not the identity block.
screenshot_context.verifier_justification: Baseline said there was no evidence the specific water record was loaded. Screenshot 1 directly contradicts that: it shows the Water record and the correct CAS. Even though the URL/ID string is not visible, the on-page identity (Water + CAS 7732-18-5) is sufficient to confirm the correct record was accessed.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot shows a NIST page header reading “NIST Chemistry WebBook, SRD 69” and the page title “Water.” In the identity section, it shows “CAS Registry Number: 7732-18-5,” which corresponds to the water record. No full URL is visible in the screenshot, but the displayed CAS number matches the ID hinted by the context (C7732185).
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: The screenshot supports that the agent is on the NIST Chemistry WebBook record for water. While the exact URL/ID string “ID=C7732185” is not visible in the image, the page clearly is the Water entry on NIST WebBook and shows CAS 7732-18-5, consistent with the specified record.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Agent claims use of the specific URL with ID=C7732185; the screenshot does not display the URL, so that exact ID cannot be visually confirmed. However, the record content (Water with CAS 7732-18-5) aligns with the intended record.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot shows a section of a NIST Chemistry WebBook-style page with headings and link lists including: “Other data available:” with items like “Condensed phase thermochemistry data”, “Phase change data”, “Reaction thermochemistry data: reactions 1 to 50, reactions 51 to 100, … reactions 1351 to 1360”, “Gas phase ion energetics data”, “IR Spectrum”, “Mass spectrum (electron ionization)”, “Gas Chromatography”, and “Fluid Properties”. Below that is “Data at other public NIST sites:” with links such as “Microwave spectra (on physics lab web site)”, “Electron-Impact Ionization Cross Sections (on physics web site)”, “Gas Phase Kinetics Database”, “Reference simulation: SPC/E Water”, and “X-ray Photoelectron Spectroscopy Database, version 5.0”. It also shows “Options: Switch to calorie-based units” and “Data at NIST subscription sites:” with “NIST / TRC Web Thermo Tables, ‘lite’ edition …” and “professional edition …”. The screenshot does not display the chemical name ‘Water’, the record ID, or the URL bar.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: The screenshot is consistent with being on a NIST WebBook compound record page, but it does not visibly confirm this is specifically the water record with ID=C7732185. There is a link mentioning “Reference simulation: SPC/E Water,” which suggests the topic is water-related, but the required explicit record identifier (ID=C7732185 / CAS 7732-18-5 / page title) is not shown. Therefore, the screenshot alone provides ambiguous provenance for Criterion 0.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Agent’s predicted output claims data from “https://webbook.nist.gov/cgi/cbook.cgi?ID=C7732185&Mask=1”, but the screenshot does not show the URL, the ID, or the identity section for water. The screenshot only shows the ‘Other data available’/links area, so the claim of being on the exact record cannot be verified from this image.

criteria.criterion: Report identity fields from the record: formula, molecular weight, IUPAC InChIKey, and CAS Registry Number
criteria.description: Report all four identity fields exactly as displayed in the specified NIST record: formula, molecular weight, IUPAC InChIKey, and CAS Registry Number. Full credit if all four are present and match the record (no altered punctuation/spacing). Partial credit if 1–3 fields are correct, or if minor transcription errors occur due to page rendering/visibility issues that the agent explicitly notes. No credit if most fields are missing/incorrect or correspond to a different compound.

screenshot_context.verifier_evidence: Screenshot 1 shows all four identity fields on the Water record: “Formula: H2O”; “Molecular weight: 18.0153”; “IUPAC Standard InChIKey: XLYOFNOQVPJJNP-UHFFFAOYSA-N”; “CAS Registry Number: 7732-18-5.”
screenshot_context.verifier_justification: The agent’s predicted output lists the same four values, matching the screenshot exactly. With Screenshot 1 confirming provenance and exact values, this should receive full credit.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: In the Water record, the screenshot visibly lists: “Formula: H2O”; “Molecular weight: 18.0153”; “IUPAC Standard InChIKey: XLYOFNOQVPJJNP-UHFFFAOYSA-N”; and “CAS Registry Number: 7732-18-5.”
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: The agent’s predicted output for the four identity fields matches what is visible in the screenshot: formula H2O, molecular weight 18.0153, InChIKey XLYOFNOQVPJJNP-UHFFFAOYSA-N, and CAS 7732-18-5. These appear to be transcribed exactly as displayed.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: No discrepancies between the agent’s listed identity fields and the visible values in the screenshot.

dom_model_context.verifier_evidence: DOM-model state 0 explicitly shows: 'Formula : H _{2} O', 'Molecular weight : 18.0153', 'IUPAC Standard InChIKey: XLYOFNOQVPJJNP-UHFFFAOYSA-N', and 'CAS Registry Number: 7732-18-5'. (State 0 is the relevant evidence for identity fields; state 1 does not show these lines in the provided excerpt.)
dom_model_context.verifier_justification: All four identity fields reported by the agent match the values shown in the DOM. The only issue is exact transcription of the formula formatting: the page displays it with subscript markup/spacing ('H _{2} O'), while the agent outputs plain 'H2O' with an explanatory note. This is a minor exactness deviation, so award near-full but not perfect credit.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence:
DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 0 visible content includes:
- "Formula : H _{2} O"
- "Molecular weight : 18.0153"
- "IUPAC Standard InChIKey: XLYOFNOQVPJJNP-UHFFFAOYSA-N"

evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis:
EVIDENCE_STATUS: SUPPORTED
All four required identity fields (formula, molecular weight, IUPAC Standard InChIKey, CAS Registry Number) are explicitly present in the DOM for the specified water record.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: The agent predicted output adds an explanatory parenthetical about subscripts ("H2O" with 2 as subscript) rather than reproducing the exact DOM text form "H _{2} O". The underlying value matches, but the transcription format is not exactly as displayed.

criteria.criterion: Report CODATA experimental gas-phase standard enthalpy of formation (with unit and reference)
criteria.description: Extract the CODATA experimental gas-phase standard enthalpy of formation entry (not calculated; not liquid-phase) from the specified NIST record, including (a) the numeric value with uncertainty exactly as shown, (b) the unit exactly as shown, and (c) the cited reference wording exactly as displayed. Full credit if all components are included verbatim and correspond to the CODATA experimental gas-phase entry. If the CODATA entry is not visible due to access/formatting limitations outside the agent’s control, full credit is awarded if the agent clearly reports the limitation and does not substitute non-CODATA/non-experimental/non-gas-phase values; partial credit if some components (e.g., reference) are missing despite being visible.

screenshot_context.verifier_evidence: Neither Screenshot 1 nor Screenshot 2 shows the CODATA experimental gas-phase standard enthalpy of formation entry, its uncertainty, unit, or the exact reference wording. Screenshot 1 only shows a link to “Gas phase thermochemistry data.” Screenshot 2 shows other navigation links but no thermochemistry table.
screenshot_context.verifier_justification: Because the enthalpy value/unit/reference are not visible anywhere in the screenshots and the action history shows only a scroll (no click into the gas-phase thermochemistry section), the agent’s specific enthalpy value and reference text are unsupported by evidence and appear fabricated for scoring purposes. No uncontrollable blocker is shown that would prevent accessing that section. Therefore, this criterion should be scored at 0.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot shows the Water identity section and a section labeled “Information on this page:” with a link “Gas phase thermochemistry data,” but it does not show the actual thermochemistry table/entry. No enthalpy of formation value, uncertainty, unit, or CODATA reference text is visible in this screenshot.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: The agent’s predicted output includes a CODATA experimental gas-phase standard enthalpy of formation value (“-241.826 ± 0.040 kJ/mol”) and a reference (“Cox, Wagman, et al., 1984”), but none of these details are visible in the provided screenshot. Based strictly on the screenshot, there is no evidence confirming that the agent extracted the CODATA experimental gas-phase entry or its reference from the displayed page content.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Agent reports a specific CODATA value, unit, and reference, but the screenshot only shows a navigation link to “Gas phase thermochemistry data” and does not display any CODATA enthalpy entry or reference wording. Thus the reported enthalpy details are unsupported by this screenshot.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: No thermochemistry table values are visible in the screenshot. The only thermochemistry-related text present is link text under “Other data available,” including “Condensed phase thermochemistry data,” “Phase change data,” and many “Reaction thermochemistry data” ranges. There is no visible entry showing a CODATA experimental gas-phase standard enthalpy of formation, no numeric value, no uncertainty, no unit, and no reference citation text.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: The screenshot provides no visual evidence of the CODATA experimental gas-phase enthalpy of formation entry or its reference. As a result, the agent’s reported value (and citation) cannot be confirmed against the screenshot. The page appears to be in a links/navigation section rather than the detailed thermochemistry data section required by this criterion.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Agent’s predicted output includes a specific CODATA gas-phase ΔfH°gas value, uncertainty, unit, and reference (“-241.826 ± 0.040 kJ/mol … Cox, Wagman, et al., 1984”), but none of these appear anywhere in the screenshot. The screenshot does not support or contradict the specific numbers; it simply lacks the relevant data display.

dom_model_context.verifier_evidence: DOM-model state 1 (latest) shows the header/link 'Gas phase thermochemistry data' but does not display any CODATA experimental gas-phase standard enthalpy of formation value, uncertainty, units, or reference wording. DOM-model state 0 similarly does not show the required thermochemistry table/entry—only the navigation/section label is visible.
dom_model_context.verifier_justification: The agent asserted a specific CODATA gas-phase ΔfH° value, uncertainty, units, and reference wording, but none of those are present in the provided DOM-model evidence. There is also no DOM-confirmed uncontrollable blocker preventing access to the entry; it simply was not captured/shown. Under the DOM rule, this claim is unproven (fabricated relative to the available evidence), so no credit for this criterion.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 1 includes the header “Gas phase thermochemistry data” and navigation text “Information on this page: Gas phase thermochemistry data References Notes,” but it does NOT display any enthalpy-of-formation table row/value, uncertainty, units, or any CODATA entry/reference text in the visible DOM excerpt provided.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis:
EVIDENCE_STATUS: UNKNOWN
The DOM snapshot confirms we are on a page that contains/links to “Gas phase thermochemistry data,” but the required CODATA experimental gas-phase standard enthalpy of formation entry (numeric value with uncertainty, unit, and the cited reference wording) is not present in the provided DOM evidence. Without the actual CODATA ΔfH°gas line visible in the DOM-model evidence, the agent’s reported value/unit/reference cannot be verified against this state.

criteria.criterion: Preserve exact transcription as feasible and stop after required fields
criteria.description: Preserve identifiers, numbers, uncertainty notation, units, and reference wording exactly as displayed when visible, and stop after the five required outputs (four identity fields plus the enthalpy entry including unit and reference). Full credit if transcription is exact and no extra unrequested content is added. Partial credit if minor extra content is included or if exact reproduction is impeded by visibility/rendering issues that the agent explicitly notes. No credit if substantial paraphrasing alters values/wording, or if the response materially continues beyond the stopping condition.

screenshot_context.verifier_evidence: Agent’s predicted output includes additional unrequested content beyond the five required fields (e.g., “Method: Review,” “Comment: CODATA Review value,” and extra explanatory text). Screenshots do not allow verification of exact enthalpy/reference transcription.
screenshot_context.verifier_justification: Even ignoring the unverifiable enthalpy transcription, the stopping condition was not followed: the response continued beyond the required five fields by adding extra fields and narrative. This is a controllable failure against the criterion’s ‘stop after required fields’ requirement, so only partial credit is appropriate.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot shows the identity fields (formula, molecular weight, InChIKey, CAS) and page navigation elements, but does not display any enthalpy entry or reference. The agent’s predicted output includes additional lines beyond the five requested fields, such as “Method: Review,” “Comment: CODATA Review value,” and explanatory sentences.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: For the identity fields, the agent preserves exact text as visible. However, the enthalpy transcription cannot be validated from the screenshot. Additionally, the agent did not strictly “stop after” the required fields; the predicted output adds extra unrequested content (method/comment and explanatory narrative), which conflicts with the stopping condition requirement.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: The screenshot cannot substantiate the enthalpy value/unit/reference. Also, the agent’s response continues beyond the five required fields by adding method/comment and extra explanation, whereas the task requires stopping after recording the five fields.

dom_model_context.verifier_evidence: DOM-model state 0 shows exact formatting for identity fields (notably 'Formula : H _{2} O'). No DOM evidence is available for the enthalpy entry to assess exact transcription there. The agent's output includes extra unrequested fields ('Method', 'Comment') beyond the five required fields/stopping condition.
dom_model_context.verifier_justification: The response does not adhere to the stopping condition because it adds extra fields (Method/Comment). Also, the formula was not transcribed in the exact on-page format. Given these are controllable formatting/constraint issues (even though relatively minor), award partial credit.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 0 supports exact text for the four identity fields, but does not include the CODATA enthalpy entry. The agent predicted output also includes additional non-required lines (e.g., "Method: Review", "Comment: CODATA Review value").
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis:
EVIDENCE_STATUS: PARTIAL
The agent output includes the five requested categories, but (a) exact transcription is not fully preserved for the formula formatting as displayed in the DOM ("H _{2} O" vs "H2O"), (b) the CODATA thermochemistry components are not verifiable from the provided DOM snapshot, and (c) the response continues beyond the stopping condition by adding extra fields (method/comment).
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Extra unrequested content beyond the five required fields (method/comment). Formula formatting not exactly as displayed in DOM. Enthalpy/unit/reference not evidenced in the provided DOM snapshot.
